title: Bodies, positions and the two-body distance in the leading-order witness geometry

key_results.statement: For self-adjoint $Y_1,Y_2$ on $\mathcal H_c$ with $d_c=\dim\mathcal H_c$, the orbits $e^{-iY_j\lambda}\chi$ are the same state for every $\lambda$ iff $(Y_1-Y_2)Y_1^n\chi=\mu_0Y_1^n\chi$ for $n=0,\dots,d_c-1$, with $\mu_0=\langle Y_1\rangle-\langle Y_2\rangle$; then $e^{-iY_2\lambda}\chi=e^{i\mu_0\lambda}e^{-iY_1\lambda}\chi$.

One body (S1): $\lvert\Psi(\lambda)\rangle=\lvert\beta\rangle\otimes\lvert E_\beta(\lambda)\rangle$ with $\lvert E_\beta(\lambda)\rangle=e^{-iK_\beta\lambda}\lvert\chi\rangle$, $V_{\{b\}}=\lvert\beta\rangle\langle\beta\rvert$ and $V_{\{c\}}=\lvert E_\beta\rangle\langle E_\beta\rvert$; the body is localized at $[\beta]_0$ for every $\lambda$ and never correlated with the medium, whose state is pure.

One body (S1): two places $\beta,\beta'$ give the same medium state for every $\lambda$ iff $(K_\beta-K_{\beta'})K_\beta^n\chi=(\langle K_\beta\rangle-\langle K_{\beta'}\rangle)K_\beta^n\chi$ for all $n$, iff $W(\beta,\beta';\lambda)=1$ for all $\lambda$; they give the same state at leading order iff $u_\beta=u_{\beta'}$, i.e. $[\beta]_0=[\beta']_0$, and $1-\lvert\langle E_{\beta'}\vert E_\beta\rangle\rvert^2=\lambda^2d_0(\beta,\beta')^2+O(\lambda^3)$; the first condition implies the second, not conversely.

Two bodies (S2): $\lvert\Psi(\lambda)\rangle=\lvert\beta_1\beta_2\rangle_{c_T}\otimes\lvert E_{\beta_1\beta_2}(\lambda)\rangle$ with $\lvert E_{\beta_1\beta_2}(\lambda)\rangle=e^{-iK_{\beta_1\beta_2}\lambda}\lvert\chi\rangle$ and $K_{h_1h_2}=K_{h_1}+K_{h_2}-\Delta$; for every $\lambda$ the pair stays localized at $\{[\beta_1]_0,[\beta_2]_0\}$, is not correlated with the medium, and the medium state is pure.

Localized pair: $D=d_0([\beta_1]_0,[\beta_2]_0)=\lVert u_{\beta_1}-u_{\beta_2}\rVert$, independent of $\lambda$; the positions (as an unordered pair) and $D$ are well defined, independent of the description labels, of the split (12.6) and of $\Delta$.

Under the contract split (12.6), $C$ and $K_{h_1h_2}$ are unchanged and every record vector is translated by the same vector, $u_h\to u_h+w$ with $w=\tilde X\lvert\chi\rangle$; hence $\sim_0$, the points $[h]_0$, $d_0$, the configuration and $D$ are unchanged.

For $\beta_1\neq\beta_2$: $V_{\{b_1\}}=V_{\{b_2\}}=\tfrac12(\lvert\beta_1\rangle\langle\beta_1\rvert+\lvert\beta_2\rangle\langle\beta_2\rvert)$, $H_V=\{\beta_1,\beta_2\}$, $W(\beta_1,\beta_2)=0$, $\alpha=\pi/2$; for $\beta_1=\beta_2=\beta$ the view is $\lvert\beta\rangle\langle\beta\rvert$; these data do not depend on $D$.

The pair view is pure, $V_{\{b_1,b_2\}}=\lvert\beta_1\beta_2\rangle_{c_T}\langle\beta_1\beta_2\rvert_{c_T}$, with $p_{(\beta_1,\beta_2)}=p_{(\beta_2,\beta_1)}=\tfrac12$ and $W\bigl((\beta_1,\beta_2),(\beta_2,\beta_1)\bigr)=1$, so $X_V$ is one point; for $\beta_1\neq\beta_2$ the witness data of both views do not depend on $D$, $\lambda$, $\Delta$, $\chi$ or the $K_h$, so $D$ cannot be seen in the views of the bodies.

For two starts $(\beta_1,\beta_2)$ and $(\beta_1',\beta_2')$: $1-\lvert\langle E_{\beta_1'\beta_2'}\vert E_{\beta_1\beta_2}\rangle\rvert^2=\lambda^2\lVert u_{\beta_1}+u_{\beta_2}-u_{\beta_1'}-u_{\beta_2'}\rVert^2+O(\lambda^3)=\lambda^2d_0\bigl((\beta_1,\beta_2),(\beta_1',\beta_2')\bigr)^2+O(\lambda^3)$, with the pair-geometry distance (12.13); $\Delta$ cancels.

Two starts give the same medium state at leading order iff $u_{\beta_1}+u_{\beta_2}=u_{\beta_1'}+u_{\beta_2'}$, iff $d_0\bigl((\beta_1,\beta_2),(\beta_1',\beta_2')\bigr)=0$, i.e. iff their joint places are the same point of the pair geometry (12.13) (for $c_T=-1$, (12.13) is used only as a formula).

If $K_{\beta_1}+K_{\beta_2}-K_{\beta_1'}-K_{\beta_2'}=\mu\mathbb 1$ with $\mu\in\mathbb R$, then $\lvert E_{\beta_1'\beta_2'}(\lambda)\rangle=e^{i\mu\lambda}\lvert E_{\beta_1\beta_2}(\lambda)\rangle$ for all $\lambda$: a sufficient condition for the same medium state for every $\lambda$, independent of $\Delta$; the necessary and sufficient condition is (15.2) with $Y_1=K_{\beta_1\beta_2}$, $Y_2=K_{\beta_1'\beta_2'}$.

The leading-order medium state distinguishes all realizable configurations iff the pair vector $s(x_1,x_2)=u_{x_1}+u_{x_2}$ is injective on them: $u_{x_1}+u_{x_2}=u_{x_1'}+u_{x_2'}\Rightarrow\{x_1,x_2\}=\{x_1',x_2'\}$, i.e. no two distinct realizable configurations share the midpoint $\tfrac12(u_{x_1}+u_{x_2})$ (realizable: all multisets of background points for $c_T=+1$; $x_1\neq x_2$, or $x_1=x_2$ with at least two places in $x_1$, for $c_T=-1$); when it holds, the configuration and $D$ are functions of the leading-order medium state, and therefore also of the exact one.
Line ($K_{h_i}=iX$, $\sigma_X>0$): every place is its own background point, $d_0(h_i,h_j)=\sigma_X\lvert i-j\rvert$ and $D(\{h_{i_1},h_{i_2}\})=\sigma_X\lvert i_1-i_2\rvert$.

Line with $\Delta=0$: two configurations give the same medium state (for every $\lambda$, and at leading order) iff $i_1+i_2=i_1'+i_2'$; $D$ is a function of the medium state only for $n=2$ ($c_T=+1$) or $n\le3$ ($c_T=-1$), since for larger $n$ distinct configurations with equal sum have different $D$ ($\{h_1,h_3\}$ and $\{h_2,h_2\}$ for $c_T=+1$, $n\ge3$; $\{h_1,h_4\}$ and $\{h_2,h_3\}$ for $c_T=-1$, $n\ge4$).

Window ($w_i=\{i,\dots,i+m-1\}$, $e_l$ the place of $c$ with only bit $l$ set): $u_{h_i}=\sum_{l\in w_i}e_l$, every place is its own background point, $d_0(h_i,h_j)=\sqrt{\lvert w_i\triangle w_j\rvert}=\sqrt{2\min(\lvert i-j\rvert,m)}$ and $D=\sqrt{2\min(\lvert i_1-i_2\rvert,m)}$.

Window: two configurations give the same medium state (for every $\lambda$, or at leading order) iff $\{i_1,i_2\}=\{i_1',i_2'\}$; (15.14) holds for both families and all $n,m$, so $D$ is a function of the medium state, with $D^2=4m-\lVert s\rVert^2$.

definitions.name: Configuration of a pair of bodies
Record vector of a background point
Joint contract operator of two bodies
Pair record vector of a configuration

open_issues: D is defined through the background. For c_T = −1, whether the background is the geometry of a view is out of scope. The views of the bodies (15.9), (15.10) do not contain D, and at leading order the medium records only the pair vector s (the midpoint), not D in general.
For (S2) the exact criterion is given only in operator form, (15.2) with the joint operator K(β1, β2); it is not reduced to record vectors.
Localized starts never become correlated with the medium. Delocalized starts, motion, more bodies and several types are out of scope.

consistency_checks.check: β1 = β2 = β with c_T = +1: the pair state (15.6) reduces to the one-body state (15.3) with K_β replaced by 2K_β − Δ, the view (15.9) reduces to the localized one-body view, D = 0, and the leading-order rate for {x,x} against {x′,x′} is 2 d_0(x,x′), in agreement with (15.4) for record vectors 2u and with (12.13)

Change of split (12.6) and dimensions: C, the joint contract operator and the medium state are unchanged, the shift u → u + w leaves (15.7), the differences in (15.11) and (15.14) unchanged, and λ·d_0, λ·D and the right sides of (15.1) and (15.11) are dimensionless

Window with m = 1: the record vectors e_i are orthonormal, d_0 = √2 for i ≠ j agrees with the direct value of ‖e_i − e_j‖, ν is the indicator of the multiset {i1, i2} and so fixes the configuration, and D² = 4 − ‖s‖² gives 0 for {i,i} and 2 for {i,j}
